stats.fact: CVE-2026-26030 is a CRITICAL (CVSS 9.9) Remote Code Execution vulnerability in Microsoft Semantic Kernel Python SDK, specifically within the InMemoryVectorStore filter functionality (CWE-94: Code Injection).
CVE-2026-26030 affects Semantic Kernel Python SDK versions prior to 1.39.4. The fix was released in python-1.39.4 on February 19, 2026.
CVE-2026-25592 is a CRITICAL (CVSS 9.9) Arbitrary File Write vulnerability in Microsoft Semantic Kernel .NET SDK SessionsPythonPlugin (CWE-22: Path Traversal).
CVE-2026-25592 affects Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Plugins.Core versions prior to 1.71.0 and pip semantic-kernel versions prior to 1.39.3. Fix released February 6, 2026.

Both CVEs share the same CVSS vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H — Network attack vector, Low complexity, Low privileges required, No user interaction, Changed scope, full CIA impact.
CVE-2026-26030 was discovered by amiteliahu, doredry, and urioren. CVE-2026-25592 was discovered by doredry, amiteliahu, and urioren.
The InMemoryVectorStore RCE (CVE-2026-26030) exploits filter expression evaluation — the fix blocks dangerous attribute names in filter expressions (PR #13505).
The SessionsPythonPlugin Arbitrary File Write (CVE-2026-25592) exploits DownloadFileAsync/UploadFileAsync with unvalidated localFilePath — the fix adds file upload security controls.
Semantic Kernel is Microsoft's open-source AI orchestration SDK with 28.3k GitHub stars and 4.7k forks, used to build, orchestrate, and deploy AI agents and multi-agent systems.
A Docker-based PoC lab (sk-cve-lab) exists on GitHub demonstrating the CVE-2026-26030 exploit in an ethical, network-isolated environment.
Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index reports 66% of surveyed AI users have more time for high-value work, and 16% are 'Frontier Professionals' using agents for multi-step workflows.

angles: Lead with the severity: both CVEs are CRITICAL 9.9 — Semantic Kernel users must prioritize patching immediately, not treat these as routine updates.
Frame the two CVEs as a pattern: one Python-side (code injection via vector store filters), one .NET-side (path traversal via agent function calling). Both exploit agent-trust boundaries.

Position the guide as a practical remediation playbook: inventory your Semantic Kernel version, check for InMemoryVectorStore usage, check for SessionsPythonPlugin usage, apply patches, add workaround filters.

Explain the technical root cause accessibly: CVE-2026-26030 = filter expressions evaluated with dangerous attribute access (eval-like); CVE-2026-25592 = agent function calling allows arbitrary file paths without sanitization.

Include a risk assessment matrix: which deployments are most exposed (production agent systems using vector stores, .NET agents with file I/O plugins), which are least (non-production, no vector store usage).
Add a 'defense in depth' section: beyond patching, add Function Invocation Filters, input validation, network segmentation, and monitoring for suspicious filter expressions or file operations.
Compare with other AI framework CVEs (LangChain, AutoGen, etc.) to show Semantic Kernel is not uniquely vulnerable — but its criticality demands attention.
Include a migration/upgrade checklist: pip install --upgrade semantic-kernel, NuGet package updates, verify with version checks, test filter functionality post-upgrade.
Connect to the broader Microsoft Agent Framework narrative: as Semantic Kernel users migrate to Agent Framework, they should audit for these vulnerabilities during migration.
Add a FAQ section: 'Do I need to worry if I don't use InMemoryVectorStore?', 'Is the .NET SDK affected differently than Python?', 'Can I use a WAF to mitigate these?'
